claim:
Let \(1<q<2\), \(0<\omega<1\), and let \(X=d^{(2)}(\omega,q)\) be the real two-dimensional Lorentz sequence space
\[
\|(x_1,x_2)\|_X=\bigl((x_1^*)^q+\omega(x_2^*)^q\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where \(x_1^*\ge x_2^*\ge0\) is the decreasing rearrangement of \((|x_1|,|x_2|)\). Put
\[
\rho=\omega^{1/(2-q)}.
\]
Then the dual space has exact Ptolemy constant
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X^*)
=
(1+\rho^2)^{(2-q)/q}
\max\left\{1,\frac{2}{(1+\omega)^{2/q}}\right\}.
\]
This is exactly the known value of \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)\). Consequently,
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(d^{(2)}(\omega,q)\right)
=
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(d^{(2)}(\omega,q)^*\right)
\]
for every \(0<\omega<1\) and every \(1\le q<\infty\).

correctness.rationale: The dual norm is obtained by maximizing a linear functional over the ordered Lorentz unit ball. For \(p=q/(q-1)\), the unconstrained Hölder optimizer is feasible exactly when \(m\le\omega M\), giving the first branch, and otherwise the optimum is the diagonal boundary point. The ratio of this dual norm to the Euclidean norm has one critical point \(\rho=\omega^{1/(2-q)}\) on the first branch and is increasing on the second. This gives exact global comparison constants. Euclidean Ptolemy supplies the upper bound, and two explicit triples attain it on the two sides of the phase boundary \(\omega=2^{q/2}-1\).
